questions.question_text: In $12^{7}$, which number is the base?

options.why: Named the small raised number, which is the index, not the base.
Multiplied $12\times 7$ instead of naming one of the two parts.
Added $12+7$ instead of naming one of the two parts.

questions.solution_text:
$12^{7}$
The base is $12$ and the index is $7$.

options.why: Swapped the base and the index, using the count as the base.
Counted the six multiplication signs instead of the seven factors.
Multiplied the base by the number of factors instead of writing a power.

questions.question_text: Which is the expanded form of $5^{3}$?

options.why: Swapped the base and the index, expanding $3^{5}$ instead of $5^{3}$.
Treated the index as repeated addition instead of repeated multiplication.
Multiplied the base by the index instead of expanding the power.
Attached each count to the wrong base.
Counted the three multiplication signs between the $7$s instead of the four $7$s.
Multiplied the two different bases together and counted all six factors.

questions.question_text: In $2^{5}\times 7$, what is the index of the $7$?

options.why: Assumed that no index written means an index of zero.
Copied the index belonging to the other base.
Repeated the number itself as its own index.

questions.question_text: Write $3\times 2\times 3\times 7\times 2\times 3$ in index form, with the bases in increasing order.

options.why: Attached the count of $3$s to the $2$ and the count of $2$s to the $3$.
Counted only the first two $3$s and missed the third one at the end of the product.
Multiplied the three different bases together and used the total number of factors as the index.

questions.question_text: $3^{4}\times 6^{2}$ is written in expanded form. How many numbers are multiplied together altogether?

options.why: Multiplied the two indices instead of adding them.
Counted the two powers rather than the factors they stand for.
Counted only the four factors in $3^{4}$ and ignored the two $6$s.

questions.question_text: $3\times 3\times 3\times 3$ is written in index form using base $9$. What is the index?

options.why: Kept the count of $3$s instead of counting the groups of two $3$s.
Divided the new base $9$ by $3$ rather than counting the groups.
Used the new base as the index as well.
